picture.content: Tangent velocity arrow decomposed into signed horizontal and vertical component arrows.

word.content: Velocity is a directed state built from components; speed is only its nonnegative magnitude.

translation_checks: Given signed v_x and v_y, draw the tangent velocity arrow and state why a negative v_y does not make speed negative.

picture.content: Five-stage trajectory timeline with constant v_x arrows, signed v_y arrows and downward g at every stage.

word.content: Horizontal velocity stays constant while vertical velocity decreases through zero and becomes negative; gravity remains downward.

symbol.content: v_x=u_x; v_y>0 rising, v_y=0 apex, v_y<0 falling; g downward

translation_checks: For a marked trajectory stage, infer the signs of v_x and v_y and identify whether the stage can be the apex without setting g to zero.

picture.content: Current tangent velocity with signed v_x/v_y components and angle phi from the positive horizontal.

word.content: Instantaneous direction comes from the current signed component pair, not from reusing the launch angle.

symbol.content: phi from (v_x,v_y), with the sign/quadrant preserved

translation_checks: Translate a falling-branch component triangle into a negative/below-horizontal direction and recover phi from the signed components.

picture.content: Velocity component triangle whose hypotenuse is speed, compared with the apex state where the vertical leg is zero.

word.content: Speed is the magnitude of velocity; in the standard model it is minimum at the apex because only the horizontal component remains.

symbol.content: v, v_x, v_y; at apex v_y=0

translation_checks: From an apex picture, write the component state and explain algebraically why minimum speed is not zero for an oblique launch.

picture.content: Rising and falling points at one horizontal height line with equal v_x, opposite signed v_y and equal-length resultant arrows.

word.content: At the same height the speeds match, but the velocity vectors differ because the vertical component reverses direction.

translation_checks: Given two equal-height trajectory points, write both component pairs and identify exactly which quantities match and which change sign.

picture.content: Reference velocity u and instantaneous velocity v(t) shown at right angles in one shared x-y frame, with both component pairs visible.

word.content: Perpendicularity is a relation between both vectors, not a rule that one component must vanish.

translation_checks: Translate a right-angle vector picture into the signed component dot-product equation before substituting projectile time evolution.

picture.content: Trajectory with declared y=0 launch origin, target height y, apex H, constant horizontal component and vertical component at the target state.

word.content: Use vertical displacement to obtain the vertical component at the target height, then rebuild total speed with the unchanged horizontal component.

translation_checks: From a marked target height, declare the displacement origin, derive v_y^2, and then reconstruct v^2 without solving time first.
